_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for NKE retrospectives (retro/build_nke.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern); every NIKE earnings release of the period came after the close, and each call transcript was furnished by its own 8-K a few days later. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the latest call's outlook words for the current fiscal year published by AS_OF, and events published since that vintage. NIKE's fiscal year ends May 31. Values are as reported, per share on the basis of the filing that published them; a vintage takes each year from the latest 10-K that reports it, and eps_published / shares_published give such a year's own publication date, so a stock split ('splits') restates exactly the per-share facts published before its effective date. NIKE gave no revenue, EPS or pre-tax margin guide in numbers in any filing of the period: the outlook on its calls is in words, gross-margin changes at times in basis points ('guides' hold them, display only). A print's margins and growth rates are derived from the published income statement and balance sheet (the raw figures are in its notes); lc_pct is the release's revenue growth less the currency effect it states, or from Q3 FY09 the growth excluding currency changes it states; eps_q is diluted EPS, excluding non-comparable items where the release publishes that figure (GAAP in the note). rule_t holds the ten annual values (FY1998-FY2007) behind the engine's signal thresholds. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing.

rule_t._doc: Rule T (retro/README.md, LOW, AAPL and NKE): for each signal its ten annual values FY1998-FY2007, each change from the latest 10-K published by 2008-01-04 that reports both years (the FY2002 10-K's eleven-year history covers FY1997-FY1999); year-end futures growth from each year's own 10-K, the only filing that reports it; reported figures, since no filing publishes gross margin or pre-tax income excluding the FY1998-FY1999 restructuring charges; XBULL = the best year, BULL = the median, BASE = the worst year, BEAR = one median-to-worst step below the worst (above, for the inventory gap, where lower is better); rounded half up to whole percent or 10 bp

futures.measure: futures orders growth, % (reported, worldwide futures and advance orders at fiscal year end)

inventory_gap.measure: year-end inventory growth less revenue growth, pp (lower is better)

pretax_margin.measure: pre-tax margin change, bp (income before income taxes / revenues)
